kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea ORANGE/WATCH - Lava flows began erupting from the north vent within Halema'uma'u yesterday, November 2, and are continuing this morning. High fountaining remains a possibility today or anytime within the next few days.
kilauea_notices.detail: Overview: Lava flows began yesterday, November 2, from the north vent in Halemaʻumaʻu and are continuing this morning. Minor deflation that began just around 1:00 p.m. yesterday has slowed and may be turning back to inflation. Seismic tremor at the summit is elevated with fluctuations in tremor associated with the beginning and end of lava overflows. SO2 emission rates are elevated. Episode 56 high fountaining remains a possibility today or anytime through November 8 based upon prior behavior once precursory flows have begun. Summit Observations: Voluminous overflows of lava began erupting from the north vent yesterday at 11:43 a.m. HST. The first two flows lasted over an hour and were highly degassed. The third overflow began at 3:35 p.m. and lasted approximately 40 minutes, forming a small but active dome fountain, which signaled the arrival of more gas-rich magma. Subsequent overflows produced dome fountains approximately 6-7 meters (20-23 feet) high. These typically lasted about 15-20 minutes with breaks of 5-15 minutes in between when lava drained back but remained visible near the top of the vent. After 29 overflows, dome fountains began decreasing around 4:00 a.m. The last few overflows this morning did not produce dome fountains, and lava appears to be retreating further into the vent, disappearing from view between overflows. There have been 42 overflows from the north vent since the start of activity yesterday. One small overflow escaped from the combined southwest vent yesterday at 4:22 p.m. and lasted less than two minutes. Strong glow could be seen from the southwest vent overnight, along with occasional spatter and flames. Background seismic tremor increased yesterday around 3:30 p.m. and remains elevated as of this morning. Periodic strong tremor bursts associated with the vigorous drain back of lava marking the end of each overflow have diminished since around 3 a.m. HST. Deformation reversed from deflationary tilt to slow inflationary tilt at that time and dome fountains began to drop in size until they were no longer present during overflows this morning. The Uēkahuna tiltmeter (UWD) had recovered a total of 18.1 microradians of tilt since the end of episode 55 by approximately 12:30 p.m. yesterday. Minor deflation began around 1:00 p.m. yesterday and continued until about 3:00 a.m. this morning. In that time, the UWD tiltmeter recorded a little over one microradian of deflationary tilt. Slow inflationary tilt has occurred since then, though this trend could change at any time. Sulfur dioxide (SO2) emission rates averaged 2200 tonnes per day (t/d) yesterday morning. Around 1:00 p.m. they began to increase, and by about 2:30 p.m. average SO2 emission rates reached approximately 4000 t/d. SO2 emissions remain elevated this morning, and strong trade winds are carrying volcanic gases southwest toward Kaʻū. Rift Zone Observations: Rates of seismicity and ground deformation remain low in the East Rift Zone and Southwest Rift Zone. SO2 emissions from the East Rift Zone remain below the detection limit. Analysis: Following episode 55 on October 17, 2026, summit tiltmeters initially recorded a typical post-fountaining recovery, with a steady upward trend that gradually slowed and was interrupted by several small fluctuations. Tilt has continued to increase slowly following a brief negative trend on October 26. While the there have been minor fluctuations in tilt over the past week, the overall tilt pattern has been a slow, steady increase until precursory overflows began yesterday, November 2. The UWD tiltmeter recorded a little over one microradian of deflationary tilt before reversing early this morning. Voluminous precursory overflows began before the UWD tiltmeter had the full 21 microradians of tilt lost during episode 55 fountaining, and it appears unlikely to reach that level of inflation with the current fluctuations related to the overflows. mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. No earthquakes occurred directly beneath Mokuʻāweoweo. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
